plans.label: Full Coverage
plans.description: Classic scene coverage pattern combining a master, an over-the-shoulder pair, a favored single, an insert, and a reaction shot for standard editorial flexibility.

shots.intent: Establish blocking, spatial relationships, and full performance for the scene as a safety and editorial spine.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame every performer in the scene with headroom and blocking space; keep the camera locked off so this shot can carry any dialogue beat in the edit.

shots.intent: Give the editor a matched shoulder shot favoring character A that motivates cutting on their dialogue and reactions.
shots.promptGuidance: Foreground character B's shoulder and ear soft in frame; keep character A's eyeline consistent with the master for clean matched cutting.

shots.intent: Mirror OTS A from the reverse side so the scene can cut cleanly between both speaking characters.
shots.promptGuidance: Match focal length, height, and eyeline of OTS A exactly, just reversed, so the pair cuts together without a jump.

shots.intent: Isolate the scene's focal character in a clean, uncluttered frame for their key line or beat.
shots.promptGuidance: Choose whichever character carries the scene's emotional weight; keep the background simple so nothing competes with their performance.

shots.intent: Highlight a specific object or detail the dialogue or blocking references, giving the editor a cutaway.
shots.promptGuidance: Fill the frame with the object referenced in the scene, such as a prop, document, or hands at work, shot tight enough to read instantly.

shots.intent: Capture a silent reaction that can be cut in to punctuate another character's line.
shots.promptGuidance: Hold on the listening character's face with no dialogue of their own; let the expression carry the beat.

plans.label: Dialogue Coverage
plans.description: Two-person conversation pattern built for seamless back-and-forth cutting: a wide master, a matched OTS pair, a matched CU pair, and a listening reaction.

shots.intent: Establish the geography of the conversation and give the editor a wide safety to return to.
shots.promptGuidance: Keep both characters fully in frame with clear negative space between them so the eyeline reads even in the wide.

shots.intent: Favor character A while keeping character B present as a foreground anchor.
shots.promptGuidance: Match lens height and distance to OTS B; character B's shoulder should occupy the same frame proportion in both shots.

shots.intent: Favor character B as the reverse of OTS A for standard shot and reverse-shot cutting.
shots.promptGuidance: Mirror OTS A's framing exactly in reverse; keep both characters' eyelines crossing believably toward each other.

shots.intent: Move into character A's face for their most important lines, isolating performance detail.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame tight from collarbone up; keep focus critically sharp on the eyes for this character's key dialogue moment.

shots.intent: Mirror CU A for character B so both speakers get equal close-up weight in the edit.
shots.promptGuidance: Match CU A's framing and eyeline height in reverse; keep lighting and lens consistent across the pair.

shots.intent: Capture a nonverbal response that can land on the other character's dialogue.
shots.promptGuidance: Hold on whichever character is listening at the scene's turning point; let silence and micro-expression do the work.

plans.label: Motion Coverage
plans.description: Coverage pattern for a moving subject, combining tracking, following, lateral, POV, aerial, and detail shots to sell speed and momentum.

shots.intent: Travel ahead of the subject to show their forward drive and the space they're moving into.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera moves backward at the subject's pace, keeping them centered; let the environment stream past on both sides.

shots.intent: Stay directly behind the subject to build urgency and put the viewer in pursuit.
shots.promptGuidance: Shoulder-height handheld directly behind the subject's back, matching their exact speed with natural sway.

shots.intent: Reveal the subject's speed and the scale of the environment they're crossing.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera moves parallel to the subject's path on a lateral track, keeping them at a consistent screen position as background scrolls past.

shots.intent: Put the viewer directly in the subject's perspective as they move.
shots.promptGuidance: Simulate the subject's own eyeline and head-bob; hands or forward motion may enter frame at the edges.

shots.intent: Pull back to show the subject's path within the full scale of the environment.
shots.promptGuidance: Rise and track from above to reveal the subject as one moving element within a much larger landscape or cityscape.

shots.intent: Isolate a physical detail of the motion itself, such as feet, wheels, or hands, for texture and rhythm.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight, fast-shutter-feeling frame on the point of contact driving the motion, such as footfall, tires, or gripping hands.

plans.label: Extreme Action
plans.description: High-impact action beat coverage: the hit, the chaos, the damage, and the aftermath, built for a fast, disorienting cut.

shots.intent: Capture the precise moment of collision or impact as the scene's punctuation point.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame tight on the point of contact at the instant of impact; the composition should read as a single decisive beat.

shots.intent: Convey chaos and disorientation as the action escalates.
shots.promptGuidance: Aggressive handheld with a canted horizon and rough camera energy; let framing feel barely in control.

shots.intent: Snap sudden attention onto a critical action detail or reaction.
shots.promptGuidance: Rapid push-in that lands hard on the subject; the speed of the move itself should feel like part of the impact.

shots.intent: Sell physical consequence through flying or scattered debris and damage detail.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight low frame on debris, dust, or damage settling in the immediate aftermath of the impact.

shots.intent: Give the surviving or dominant figure a powerful, victorious silhouette after the action peak.
shots.promptGuidance: Shoot up at the subject from near ground level so they read as commanding and larger than the chaos around them.

shots.intent: Reveal the full scale of consequence once the action has settled.
shots.promptGuidance: Crane up and back to show the entire aftermath, including damage, debris, and figures, in one settled, wide frame.

plans.label: Establishing Sequence
plans.description: Opening location sequence that moves from aerial approach down to street level and into an interior, orienting the audience in stages.

shots.intent: Introduce the location's geography from above before narrowing focus.
shots.promptGuidance: Sweeping high drone shot approaching the location, giving a sense of scale and surrounding context before descending.

shots.intent: Present the specific building or landmark that anchors the scene.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame the landmark centered and fully visible, with enough surrounding context to confirm location and time of day.

shots.intent: Bring the audience down into human scale and everyday activity at the location.
shots.promptGuidance: Handheld at pedestrian eye height, capturing foot traffic or street life that grounds the location in lived-in reality.

shots.intent: Build atmosphere through incidental detail, such as signage, weather, or activity, that isn't plot-critical.
shots.promptGuidance: Slow pan across a texture-rich element of the environment; this shot should feel observational, not narratively urgent.

shots.intent: Pinpoint a specific sign, address, or object that confirms exact location for the audience.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight, legible frame on the specific detail, such as a street sign, door number, or plaque, that answers where we are.

shots.intent: Transition the audience from exterior to interior, completing the sequence's arrival.
shots.promptGuidance: Push in through a doorway or threshold as the subject enters, carrying momentum from exterior into interior space.

plans.label: Surveillance Coverage
plans.description: Voyeuristic, monitored coverage pattern that keeps the audience at a technological remove of cameras, lenses, and screens rather than direct presence.

shots.intent: Establish the clinical, watched feeling of a fixed overhead security perspective.
shots.promptGuidance: Mount the camera high in a corner position with slight wide-angle distortion, as if bolted to a wall; keep it perfectly locked off.

shots.intent: Observe the subject from a concealed distance with compressed, voyeuristic framing.
shots.promptGuidance: Use heavy compression and shallow depth of field consistent with a long telephoto lens shooting from far away, unnoticed.

shots.intent: Reinforce the sense of covert observation by shooting through a partial foreground obstruction.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame the subject partially blocked by foreground elements like blinds, foliage, or a doorframe, as if glimpsed rather than shown.

shots.intent: Show the surveillance footage as viewed by a watching character, doubling the sense of observation.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame a monitor or screen displaying the surveillance feed, with scan lines, timestamp, or screen glow visible in the shot.

shots.intent: Track the subject from a discreet trailing distance as if being followed.
shots.promptGuidance: Stay well behind the subject with obstructions and crowd cover between camera and target, holding a cautious following distance.

shots.intent: Deliver a freeze-frame-like still that feels pulled directly from recorded footage for evidence or reveal.
shots.promptGuidance: Compose like a paused video frame, with slight motion blur or grain, timestamp-ready, as if captured mid-action from the feed.

plans.label: Entrance Coverage
plans.description: Character entrance pattern that builds anticipation through a doorway reveal, a hero approach, onlooker reactions, and a powerful final angle.

shots.intent: Build anticipation as the door opens and the character is first glimpsed.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame the doorway centered with the character emerging from shadow or backlight into visibility; hold the reveal a beat before movement.

shots.intent: Give the entering character a commanding, hero-scaled approach toward camera.
shots.promptGuidance: Shoot from a slightly low angle as the character walks directly toward the lens, filling the frame progressively with confidence.

shots.intent: Capture how the room or a key onlooker responds to the entrance.
shots.promptGuidance: Hold on the onlooker's face at the moment of recognition or surprise; the entering character may be off-screen or soft in the background.

shots.intent: Reorient the audience to how the entrance changes the space and the people already in it.
shots.promptGuidance: Pan or reframe from the entrance point across the room to show how attention shifts and bodies reposition.

shots.intent: Highlight an object or gesture the entering character carries that signals intent or status.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight insert on the hand, prop, or object central to the character's entrance, such as a weapon, gift, badge, or key detail.

shots.intent: Cement the character's authority or dominance once fully arrived in the space.
shots.promptGuidance: Shoot up from below eye level with the character filling the frame, expression settled and in control of the room.

plans.label: Parallel Action
plans.description: Intercut two-location pattern that builds tension by crosscutting parallel masters, tension close-ups, and synced details before converging.

shots.intent: Establish the geography and stakes of location A before crosscutting begins.
shots.promptGuidance: Wide, stable frame of location A that clearly reads the space, characters, and what's at stake there.

shots.intent: Establish location B as the parallel counterpart to A, ready to be intercut against it.
shots.promptGuidance: Match the visual grammar of A-Master in framing and stability so the two locations feel like they exist in the same story clock.

shots.intent: Raise stakes at location A through a tight, urgent close-up as events escalate.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight, slightly tense framing on the key character in A; expression and breathing should signal rising pressure.

shots.intent: Mirror the escalation at location B so both threads climb in tension together.
shots.promptGuidance: Match the intensity and framing of A-Tension CU so crosscutting between the two feels rhythmically equal.

shots.intent: Show a specific action or object at location A that the audience must track for the payoff.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight insert on the critical action in A, such as a countdown, a lock, or hands working, timed to feel urgent.

shots.intent: Mirror A's detail insert at location B, setting up the synchronized payoff between both threads.
shots.promptGuidance: Match the framing and urgency of A-Detail Insert so the two inserts read as simultaneous when intercut.

shots.intent: Provide a connective beat, such as a clock, phone, or signal, that ties both locations to the same moment in time.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame a shared reference point, such as a countdown display or communication device, that could belong to either thread.

shots.intent: Bring both storylines together in a single frame as the parallel action resolves.
shots.promptGuidance: Crane to a wide vantage that finally unites both locations or characters in one composition, paying off the crosscut.

plans.label: Dance Sequence
plans.description: Performance coverage pattern for a dance or choreographed movement piece, built around a full-body master, moving camera work, a rhythmic close-up, and a finale wide.

shots.intent: Capture the complete choreography and body language in one uninterrupted frame.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame the dancer fully from head to feet with room to move in every direction; keep the camera locked so the full performance reads clearly.

shots.intent: Match the dancer's movement to make the camera feel like a dance partner.
shots.promptGuidance: Track laterally or circularly at the dancer's own tempo, keeping them centered as the camera moves in rhythm with the choreography.

shots.intent: Isolate the percussive detail of footwork or hand gesture that drives the piece's rhythm.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight frame on feet striking the floor or hands articulating a gesture, timed to the beat for rhythmic editorial cutting.

shots.intent: Reveal the geometric shape and spacing of the choreography from directly above.
shots.promptGuidance: Shoot straight down to show the dancer's floor pattern and symmetry, emphasizing the shapes the movement traces.

shots.intent: Showcase a single standout movement or expression in extended, elevated detail.
shots.promptGuidance: Slow, graceful orbit around the dancer at their movement's peak moment, built to be slowed in post for maximum visual impact.

shots.intent: Close the sequence by pulling back to the full stage or space as the performance ends.
shots.promptGuidance: Pull back from the dancer's final pose to reveal the complete performance space, landing on a settled closing frame.

plans.label: Angle Coverage
plans.description: Systematic rotation around a static subject through six standard angles, giving the editor full flexibility to choose the most flattering or dramatic perspective.

shots.intent: Present the subject's most direct, neutral read for baseline coverage.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera square-on to the subject's face at eye level; keep expression and framing neutral and evenly lit.

shots.intent: Offer a more dimensional, flattering angle than the flat front for editorial variety.
shots.promptGuidance: Rotate roughly 45 degrees from center so both the face and a sense of depth toward the far shoulder are visible.

shots.intent: Capture the subject's pure side silhouette for a distinct graphic option.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera at exactly 90 degrees to the subject's facing direction, showing only the profile line of the face and body.

shots.intent: Show the subject from behind and around, useful for reveals or following context.
shots.promptGuidance: Position roughly 45 degrees behind the subject so the back and a hint of the far cheek are visible.

shots.intent: Provide a full rear view, useful for anonymity, mystery, or POV setups.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera directly behind the subject; frame should read the back of the head and body with no facial features visible.

shots.intent: Offer a diminishing or observational perspective distinct from the eye-level set.
shots.promptGuidance: Elevate the camera above the subject's eyeline looking down, keeping the same subject distance as the other angles for a clean set.

plans.label: Orbit
plans.description: Six-position orbital pass around the subject at varied heights, generating a full circular coverage set from low to overhead.

shots.intent: Begin the orbit with a grounded, slightly heroic read of the subject's front.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera below eye level arcing across the subject's front, giving an empowered, monumental feel to open the sequence.

shots.intent: Pass across the subject's side at a neutral height for a balanced, natural read.
shots.promptGuidance: Arc smoothly past the subject's profile at their own eye height, maintaining consistent radius and speed.

shots.intent: Shift upward to reveal more of the subject's surroundings while still circling.
shots.promptGuidance: Raise the camera above eye level while continuing the arc, angling down slightly to bring more environment into frame.

shots.intent: Complete the vertical range of the orbit with a top-down circling pass.
shots.promptGuidance: Position the camera near-directly above the subject, circling slowly to reveal the top-down shape and surrounding layout.

shots.intent: Continue the circle to a low rear angle for a mysterious or vulnerable read.
shots.promptGuidance: Camera below eye level arcing behind the subject, catching the back and shoulders from a grounded, slightly concealed vantage.

shots.intent: Return to the front at neutral height to close the orbit and complete the circle.
shots.promptGuidance: Finish the arc back at the subject's front at eye level, matching the opening shot's height to close the loop cleanly.

plans.label: Story Beats
plans.description: Six-beat narrative arc pattern that moves a scene from setup through inciting detail, confrontation, escalation, climax, and resolution.

shots.intent: Establish the scene's normal world and status quo before disruption.
shots.promptGuidance: Wide, calm framing showing characters and setting in their ordinary state, with visual room for something to change.

shots.intent: Introduce the specific object, message, or event that disrupts the status quo.
shots.promptGuidance: Tight insert on the precise trigger, such as a note, a sound source, or an arriving object, that the rest of the scene will react to.

shots.intent: Bring characters into direct conflict or dialogue as the disruption is addressed.
shots.promptGuidance: Frame the opposing characters or character-and-obstacle together in the same shot to establish direct confrontation.

shots.intent: Intensify the emotional or physical stakes as the conflict builds toward its peak.
shots.promptGuidance: Move tighter and add handheld energy as tension rises; framing should feel less controlled than the confrontation shot.

shots.intent: Hit the scene's highest point of tension or revelation in its most intense frame.
shots.promptGuidance: Push into an extreme close-up on the pivotal expression or action at the exact peak moment of the scene.

shots.intent: Release tension by pulling back to show the aftermath and new status quo.
shots.promptGuidance: Pull the camera back out to a wide, settled frame that shows where characters land once the scene's conflict resolves.
